summary:
## GDP Growth Uplifted to 3.5%

International investment banks have raised their forecast for Korea's economic growth this year to an average of 3.5%, marking six consecutive months of upward revisions. Leading global financial institutions representing eight major firms now project Korea's real gross domestic product will expand at this pace, driven primarily by robust semiconductor export performance. The outlook for next year has also been revised upward to 2.8%, up 0.3 percentage points from August projections and approaching the Bank of Korea's own estimate of 2.9%. This consistent upgrading of growth forecasts reflects international confidence in Korea's economic resilience and export competitiveness.

## Current Account Surplus Accelerates

Korea's current account surplus is expected to expand faster than nominal GDP growth, with the surplus-to-GDP ratio forecast averaging 17.5%, up 1.5 percentage points from the previous month. This exceptional external balance reflects Korea's strong export performance, particularly in high-value semiconductors, offsetting domestic consumption patterns. The widening current account surplus has become a key indicator of Korea's competitive position in global markets, though it also raises questions about domestic demand dynamics and the sustainability of export-driven growth models.

## Stock Markets Consolidate Amid Global Volatility

The KOSPI index opened down 1.0 percent at 6,860 points on October 7th, though subsequently recovered to trade around 6,900 as markets showed signs of stabilization. The KOSDAQ index declined 1.00 point, or 0.11 percent, to close at 893.29. The Korean won weakened by 7.8 won against the dollar during the week, settling at 1,350.6 won per dollar. Despite record highs in US stock indices—with the S&P 500 and NASDAQ reaching all-time peaks—Korean investors remained cautious, reflecting concerns about elevated US Treasury yields and global economic uncertainty that had pressured Asian equities.

## US Treasury Yields Stabilize Temporarily

US Treasury yields showed signs of moderating from recent highs, with the 10-year yield trading below 5.3 percent as market participants digested mixed economic signals from America. Third-quarter corporate earnings expectations and gradually easing monetary policy concerns provided some support for equity markets globally. However, the September FOMC minutes scheduled for release this week are expected to provide crucial guidance on future US monetary policy direction, potentially influencing both bond and equity markets. The volatility in global bond markets remains a critical watch point for Korean investors, as yield fluctuations directly impact foreign investment flows into Korean securities.

## Housing Crisis Deepens for Young Adults

Seoul's apartment prices have now risen for 86 consecutive weeks, reaching record duration for the nation's longest consecutive price appreciation streak. Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Lee Hyung-il acknowledged this prolonged surge with concern, stating he "feels the weight" of the situation while pledging to maximize housing supply efforts. Specifically, Seoul's building permits and construction starts surged 40.0 percent during the first eight months of 2026 compared to the same period last year. However, the immediate housing crisis confronting young people centers on soaring monthly rental rates. In Shinlim, a historic district for examination prep students, a mere 30-square-meter room now costs 1 million won monthly. Over the past five years, the proportion of sub-30-square-meter properties commanding monthly rent above 1 million won has increased sixfold. Among university districts, even 5-pyeong (16.5-square-meter) units are renting for 1.2 million won monthly, reflecting an acute affordability crisis for Korea's youth demographic.

## Government Pledges 1.19 Million Public Housing Units

To address housing affordability, the government announced plans to supply 1.19 million public housing units, with 77.0 percent targeted for the Seoul metropolitan area by 2030. Construction commencement is prioritized to achieve these targets within the specified timeframe. This massive public housing initiative represents the government's most significant intervention in the residential market, though implementation challenges remain substantial given current construction capacity and land availability constraints.

## Jeonse Fraud Victims Receive Payment Guarantee

Starting November 13th, victims of jeonse fraud—a deposit-based rental system unique to Korea—will receive minimum guaranteed payments ensuring recovery of at least one-third of their pledged deposits. The special legislation supporting fraud victims was finalized through executive decree, enabling claims to be filed with Korea Housing Finance Corporation with payment decisions issued within 90 days. Victims are eligible for minimum support funds up to 50 million won, addressing one of Korea's most pressing social issues that has devastated renters unable to recover substantial deposits.

## Battery Industry Shifts Strategy Amid Technology Race

The domestic battery sector is experiencing strategic recalibration as sodium-ion battery technology gains prominence alongside traditional lithium-ion solutions. While solid-state batteries continue attracting attention as the ultimate "dream battery" for high-performance electric vehicles and robotics, sodium-ion batteries offer superior price competitiveness for energy storage systems and mass-market electric vehicles. POSCO Future M inked a six-year contract worth 6 trillion won to supply lithium iron phosphate cathode materials to Samsung SDI beginning next year. Additionally, Orient Jeong has successfully developed proprietary thermal-conductive polyurethane adhesive specifically engineered for electric vehicle applications, improving production efficiency while simplifying assembly processes in battery pack modules and drive motor assembly.

## Trump Administration Pressures Korea on Investment

US President Donald Trump has explicitly stated that he demanded Korea provide compensation in exchange for tariff reductions, directly linking trade concessions to investment commitments. This pressure specifically targets Korea's 350 billion dollar total investment pledge, with 150 billion dollars dedicated to shipbuilding cooperation under the MASGA project—Make American Shipbuilding Great Again. The Trump administration's approach signals that traditional trade negotiations will be increasingly transactional, requiring concrete economic commitments beyond conventional tariff agreements.

## US Fiscal Deficit Reaches Critical Levels

America's trade deficit surged to 142 trillion won in August, representing the largest shortfall since Trump's initial tariff implementation, while the US national debt has exceeded 50 quadrillion won—approximately 50 percent of GDP. According to Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank's GDP Now model, third-quarter US trade deficits could reduce economic growth by as much as 2.5 percentage points, raising serious questions about long-term fiscal sustainability for the world's largest economy.

## Market Implications and Investment Outlook

For Korean investors, the current environment presents a complex mix of opportunities and risks. Domestically, Korea's GDP growth outlook remains solid at 3.5 percent driven by semiconductor and export strength, yet this export dependency creates vulnerability to global trade tensions, particularly given Trump administration protectionism. The won's weakness at 1,350.6 per dollar may provide some export boost but increases import costs and foreign debt servicing expenses. Housing affordability remains a critical social issue that could constrain domestic consumption growth despite robust external balances. Samsung Electronics' third-quarter preliminary earnings announcement today will provide crucial signals for semiconductor sector momentum heading into year-end. Internationally, American fiscal deficits and rising Treasury yields present ongoing currency and capital flow risks that warrant cautious positioning. The resolution of US-Korea trade negotiations over the coming weeks will fundamentally determine investment strategy for Korean portfolios throughout the remainder of this year.
headline: Korea GDP Forecast Raised Again as Exports Surge, Housing Prices Climb Steadily
